prerequisites: A previous knowledge on differential and integral calculus is required (from Mathematical Analysis I course).

learning_outcomes.text: Be able to use the fundamental techniques for the analysis of DC and AC circuits.
Know the fundamental laws of electromagnetism, including the ability to analyze elementary magnetic circuits.
Have practice with basic laboratory equipment: multimeters, oscilloscopes, power supplies and signal generators.

syllabus_topics: Charge, Current and Kirchhoff’s Current Law
The Node Voltage Method and The Mesh Current Method

assessment_methods.method: Individual performance analysis in the laboratory

assessment_rules: There are two evaluation components: Individual performance analysis in the laboratory (DL) weighted at 25%, and two intermediate examinations (MT) weighted at 75%. If the classification in component MT is greater than or equal to 8.0, the final classification will be the average of component DL (25%) and component MT (75%). If the classification in component MT is smaller than 8.0, the final classification will be the classification of component MT. Minimum attendance to practical classes is required for eligibility. For special assessment or classification improvement, an oral practical examination replaces component DL and a two-hour written examination paper replaces component MT.
